label: text
text: In the House of Commons, in answer to questions, Mr. Ronald McNeill, Under Secretary for Foreign Affairs, said that the principal Powers concerned had now agreed in principle regarding the judicial commission of inquiry into Shanghai disturbances. The precise procedure to be followed was still being discussed, also the composition of the committee, but presumably the commission itself would decide which of its members would preside.

label: text
text: Captain Wedgwood Benn asked would "the British representative on the commission" favour "the appointment of a Chinese as president.

label: text
text: Mr. McNeill said that the Government desired the commission to have the advantage of a Chinese judge thereon but the matter had not been definitely decided.

label: text
text:
The Prince of Wales has sent a wireless message to the Governor-General expressing his gratitude for the wonderful hospitality of South Africa and declaring that he will always cherish the happiest recollections of the country.
He says that one of the most encouraging memories of the tour will certainly be the large numbers of happy, healthy children who greeted him everywhere and who will, he knows, realise their good fortune and grow up to be good citizens, in a land endowed with an unrivalled climate and boundless possibilities of development, with confident hope in their own future.

label: text
text: The Prince concludes: "I was very sad at leaving you all and can only say au'revoir."

text: Atlanta, (Georgia), Aug. 4. A warrant, which has been issued for the deportation of Marcus Garvey to Jamaica will be served when he is released from the Federal prison, where he is serving a term for fraudulently using the mails.

label: text
text: It is alleged that Garvey sponsored the project to 'colonise Africa with American negroes.

text: Mr. Mackenzie King, speaking at Kitchener (Ontario) repudiated the idea of Canada's annexation to the United States, saying:—"I believe that Canadians' dre concerning themselves with such a possibility about the same extent as the United States is concerning itself with annexation to the British Empire." He considered that Canada and the United States were better off as separate entities.

text:
Sun Fo arrived at Peking this afternoon accompanied by the Canton Foreign Commissioner, Mr. Fu Ping-chang. Governmental departments sent representatives to meet him.
Mr. Sun Fo is reported to have come here to make arrangements for his father's funeral, but it is stated that he will also probably discuss the Shameen affair with the Government.

label: text
text: Mr. Sun Fo, as most people will know, is the son of the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen. He was at his father's bedside when the latter died in Peking but returned to Canton subsequently.

label: text
text: Prior to Dr. Sun's departure for the North, Mr. Sun Fo had been Mayor of Canton for some time, being the first to hold that post when municipal administration was mooted.

label: text
text: In the subsequent re-organisation of the Kuomintang Government at Canton, after the Yunnanese and Kwangsi mercenaries had been expelled, Mr. Sun Fo was given the post of Minister of Communications.

label: text
text: [As reported in the “China Mail,” Mr. Fu Ping-chang (or Fu Ping-sheung, in Cantonese) is the Commissioner for Foreign Affairs in Canton. He is fairly young and belongs to Mr. Sun Fo's clique. Educated at St. Stephen's College, he graduated from the Hongkong University. Last year he took part in the negotiations regarding the Sha-meen strike.]

label: text
text: According to rumours current at the time of Mr. Sun Fo's departure from Caxton, he was going either to Shanghai, Peking or to interview Marshal Chang Tso-lin. Mr. Sun Fo is not considered to be one of the Canton radicals. When party strife was being waged in Canton, Mr. Sun's name was connected with the "Prince" party which did not see eye to eye with the allegedly Communistic party. His present mission to Peking may have even more significance than hinted in Reuter's cable, perhaps discussion with either Feng Yu-hsiang (the Christian general), Tuan Chi-jul (the Chief Executive) or Chang Tso-lin (the Mukden warlord).

label: text
text: By a proclamation issued to-day H.E. the Governor orders that the period of military service by the Hongkong Volunteer Defence Corps, which commenced on June 21, shall end at midnight to-day.

label: text
text:
The gunboat which carries money from Kongmoon to the Canton Government—such moneys being remittances which Canton has insisted must not be appropriated by local warlords—has sunk on account of an explosion in the engine room. It is stated that the gunboat was near Yungki when boiler trouble brought about a terrific explosion.
Seven of the crew were killed outright but no others were injured.

label: text
text: Tha Kongmoon-Shekki tow-boat has again been pipited while under way. No details have come to hand yet.

label: text
text: The hearing of an arms case against two Chinese, adjourned from last Saturday, was continued at the Central Magistracy yesterday with Mr. S. B. B. McElderry and Mr. R. A. D. Forrest sitting together as Magistrates.

label: text
text: Only one man was charged with unlawful possession of a loaded revolver, and he pleaded not guilty. The evidence was that the accused was challenged by Sergeant Gough and a Chinese constable who had noticed him acting in a suspicious manner near the trum terrainus at Shaukiwan. The accused was seen to throw the revolver into a nullah. The weapon was subsequently recovered by the police.

label: text
text: The accused was found guilty, and under the powers vested in them by the emergency regulations their Worships imposed a sentence of five years' hard labour.

label: text
text: The other accused was sentenced by Mr. McElderry, to six months' hard labour this morning on a charge of being a rogue and a vagabond.

label: text
text: A sad accident befell two children from the village of Lok-machau, in the New Territories, when they were returning to their home early on Monday morning after completing an errand

label: text
text:
The children were forced to seek refuge under a tree from the rain, which later developed into a violent thunderstorm.
NATIVE REPORTER AS COMPLAINANT.

label: text
text: An application made by Mr. J. A. Gordon Leask for bail was refused by the Magistrate (Mr. E. W. Hamilton) who characterised the offence as a serious one and running on a par with those perpetrated in Peking.

label: text
text:
A clap of thunder which shook the village caused uneasiness in the minds of the relatives, and as soon as the storm had abated they set out in search of the children. They found only the charred remains of the unfortunate children, as the lightning had struck both the trees and those who sought shelter at the foot.
A reporter of a vernacular newspaper was the complainant in a case at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning when a Chinese shopkeeper was charged with intimidation.

label: text
text:
According to information given by the complainant, Lau Mancho, when applying for a warrant of apprehension, he had been threatened by the accused for reporting a case concerning a night soil coolie heard before the Secretary for Chinese Affairs and had been asked to publish a different statement and an apology.
The case was adjourned until to-morrow.

text: WHAT ARE THE NAVAL YARD DOING?

label: text
text: Reports still continue to be received of strikers returning on the one hand and others being employed to take the place of strikers on the other.

label: text
text: The Dairy Farm has had a number of workers return and about 40 per cent. of old Naval Dockyard employees are now at work. The Government Civil Hospital has taken on a large number of men to replace strikers.

label: text
text: The China man learns from a reliable source that the attitude that the Naval Yard authorities are taking to returning strikers is that they should be placed on the lowest grade payment of their particular class of work only for a week or two after rejoining, the opinion being that this is sufficient to bring home to them the unlawfulness of their action in leaving. Many strikers are now reported to be earning pre-strike pay.

label: text
text: The Naval authorities refused to confirm or deny this, however, a “China Mail” representative being told that they had nothing to impart to the Press as to the attitude they were adopting.

label: text
text: A Chinese amish until recently in the employment of Mrs. Gibbieson, of No. 3, Torres Buildings, was charged before the Kowloon Magistrate this morning for leaving without notice.

label: text
text: It was stated by the complainant that the accused first left the house on June 3. She came back on July 1, worked five days and left again.

label: text
text:
Questionsed by the Magistrate as to the date on which the accused was stated to have first left, which was long before the strike commenced, the complainant stated that there had been no mistake. She said that she did not desire to press the charge, but only wished that the accused would not molest a new family since engaged by her.
His Worship discharged the accused with a warning.

label: text
text:
Because workers from Hong Kong have managed to get here by the Shekki tow boat, a striker's branch depot has been started at Chinshan, which is in Chinese territory, just outside the Macao boundary.
Instead of coming direct to Macao, the Shekki tow boat now calls at Chinshan where passengers landed. All those who want to pass the Chinese border are interrogated by a picket. It is stated that workers are not allowed to go and that others are mulcted in “fines” of $20 or $25 for the privilege of going through.

label: text
text: A case of much interest to the Chinese community was again adjourned by Mr. R. A. D. Forrest when informed this morning that the proceedings would last several hours owing to there being a number of witnesses on each side.

label: text
text: Sam Choi, an accountant of the Kwong Sang Hong Company, defended by Mr. C. A. S. Russ, and Wong Chuen, defended by Mr. C. H. Lyson, were the accused persons in the prosecution which is being conducted by Mr. T. H. King, Director of Criminal Intelligence.

label: text
text: The two accused were taken into custody for alleged stone throwing at a street lecturer, who is stated to have been delivering an oration against the strike under the auspices of the Labour Maintenance Association, and in addition to disorderly conduct they are charged with intimidation.

label: text
text: Bail for the second accused was fixed at $500. Mr. Lyson's application for a reduction was unsuccessful.

label: text
text: The case was fixed for hearing at 12 noon, to-morrow, and during the afternoon.

label: text
text: Seen this morning in connection with the departure yesterday of the Wosang for Tientsin and the Hangsang for Bangkok, Mr. Ho Leung, compradore of Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd., in reply to the question whether such movements could be taken as representing a return to anything like normal trade conditions, said that the merchants were doing their best and would continue to do so. It was hoped for instance, to get another boat away for Tientsin on Thursday or Friday, but it was impossible to forecast regarding prospects of future general movements of goods, so much hinged on Canton. The Wosang, with a cargo of rice and sugar, was the second boat that the Indo-China Steam Navigation Company had got away to Tientsin since the strike, and in all eleven had been cleared.

text: Mr. Leo D'Almada, for the defendant relative, also put it to the plaintiff that his client had been further instrumental in obtaining $40,000 for plaintiff in previous action and the loan had been made shortly after.
